slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 15, 2026
slots.body:
U.S. equity indexes closed lower across the board.
The S&P 500 ended at 7,585.51 (−34.47 points, −0.5%).
The Nasdaq Composite finished at 25,981.57 (−204.84, −0.8%).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 52,093.11 (−328.09, −0.6%), and the Russell 2000 was at 2,870.29 (−21.95, −0.8%).

The day’s high-impact U.S. data release was the NY Empire State Manufacturing Index for September: actual 7.6, versus estimate 14.75 and previous 20.6.
The print measures factory activity in the New York Fed district and landed below the expected level in the calendar data.

Sector averages on Nasdaq showed Industrials weakest at −2.1%, Utilities at −1.8%, and Consumer Cyclical and Consumer Defensive both around −1.3% to −1.4%.
Real Estate led gainers among sector averages at +0.8%, with Energy +0.4% and Communication Services +0.4%.
Technology averaged −0.7%.

Large-cap software and consumer internet names were broadly lower.
Oracle closed down 3.1% at $140.37.
Netflix fell 3.0% to $77.90.
Amazon was off 2.0% at $248.42, Microsoft −1.6% at $497.12, and Salesforce −1.5% at $255.65.
UnitedHealth declined 2.0% to $375.93, and Costco −1.9% to $901.35.

A few megacaps bucked the weak tone.
Meta Platforms rose 0.7% to $670.24.
JPMorgan Chase gained 0.7% to $352.49.
NVIDIA closed up 0.6% at $212.17.
Advanced Micro Devices was up 2.2% at $504.20, while Broadcom slipped 1.6% to $339.27.

Forgent Power Solutions reported quarterly results in the earnings calendar: EPS actual $0.25 versus estimate $0.24, revenue actual $461.67M versus estimate $429.94M.
The share price in the mega-cap set closed up 9.5% at $31.36.

Energy-linked trading showed a mixed picture in the cross-asset block.
The United States Oil Fund (USO) rose 3.3% to $161.86.
Brent crude in the data was at $107.70, down 1.0% on the session.
Gold futures (GCUSD) gained 0.8% to $4,369.30.

The U.S. dollar proxy UUP ticked up 0.2% to $28.22.
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was at $75,971.42, up 0.5%.
EUR/USD was unchanged at 1.15 in the injected quote.

Treasury yields in the latest snapshot (dated 2026-09-11 in the data) showed the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.33 percentage points.
The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) closed at 17.20, up 0.1 point (+0.6%) from the prior close.

Overseas indexes in the bundle were modestly softer: Nikkei 225 −0.1%, FTSE 100 −0.4%, Hang Seng −0.2%.
Session coverage linked U.S. equity softness to oil and the upcoming Fed decision.
